info.title: Zoop internal AI analysis transport
info.description:
Internal app-to-AI transport for the S1 analysis family (`zoop-ai-s1-1`): document-summary, document-sentiment,
semantic-verification and briefing-outlook. It is a thin, durable HTTP layer over the installed `zoop-ai` CLI; the runtime ledger
stays the only source of job state, and every state shown here is read from the runtime during the same request.

**Network.** The service binds `127.0.0.1` only. Production reach is an HTTPS reverse proxy co-located with it (same host or network
namespace) that terminates TLS, caps bodies at 2,000,000 bytes, never logs `Authorization`, and is reachable only from the app
backend's security group. That proxy is an assumption: nothing here was deployed or observed.

**Authentication.** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens are operator-issued; the service stores only SHA-256 digests. The
authenticated principal is the owner of every job it registers; there is no end-user identity in v1. A job owned by another
principal answers exactly like a missing job (404).

**Idempotency.** `Idempotency-Key` is required on submit and must equal `body.jobId`. Retry any ambiguous submit with the *same* key
and body; never mint a new jobId to retry. 202 = newly accepted (the runtime registered the job and the service made its owner
binding and dispatch intent durable); 200 = idempotent replay of an accepted job.

**Lifecycle.** `202` does not mean the job is authorized, budgeted or that any model call happened. Poll `GET /{jobId}` and follow
`next`: `wait` (a dispatch is pending or running), `fetch_result`, `recover` (call the recover route), `operator_reconcile` (stop and
escalate: an attempt has an unknown provider outcome that may have been charged; starting a new jobId accepts that cost) or `none`.
A job interrupted between two stages (some receipt stored, a later stage never sent) is never continued automatically: its dispatch
ends idle with `lastOutcome=needs_recover`, and only an explicit recover sends the next stage.
Internal `ready` is not the public `completed`: the app import must still succeed and re-check its own current authority.

**Results.** `GET /{jobId}/result` returns the runtime's `get` payload (`job`, see `ai-contract.schema.json#/$defs/JobResult`) only
while the server's *current* grant registry still permits delivery; otherwise `delivery.state` is `withheld`, `job` is null and only
content-free per-attempt `receipts` are returned for usage accounting. A live job is withheld with `reason=recipient_unproven` until the
runtime has recorded an attempt for every stage it needs, because only then is the recipient provable. `job.grant` is an execution snapshot, never current authority.

**S3 relation jobs (`/internal/v1/relation-jobs`, schema `zoop-ai-internal-relation-1`, scopes `relation.*`).** A separate family over the
installed `zoop-ai-relation` pipeline: it shares nothing with the S1 wire contract or state machine. It is off unless its
all-or-nothing server configuration group is set (otherwise every route answers 409 `execution_unavailable` after authentication). A caller
cannot name a path, fixture or registry. The body is the S3 `Submit` (`zoop-relation-s3`) naming an operator-prepared S2 extraction
job as `upstream {jobId, inputDigest}`; that pair must be listed for the calling principal in a server-owned allowlist, otherwise 403
`upstream_not_allowed` before anything is stored. `provenance.executionMode` is `replay` (authored fixtures, no network) or `live`
(`recordingKind: provider`: a real model call that costs money). A live job needs the service's live group (409 `live_unavailable` otherwise) AND an
allowlist entry that pins the runtime identity the operator approved (403 `live_not_approved` otherwise); the pipeline must freeze the job under exactly
that identity (409 `live_binding_mismatch` otherwise), and the pin is re-read before every live child and every delivery. The principal owns the job it
submits: another principal's job answers like a missing one.
The initial dispatch runs once, under the pipeline's own under-lock initial-only restriction (a job that already took its first dispatch is refused with no
effect). A child that timed out, died or answered unreadably, and a dispatch left in flight by a restarted service,
are never run again automatically (`next=recover`); a call the pipeline reserved but never saw answered ends `reconciling` and is never
resent. Only an explicit `recover` dispatches again (and, for a live job, spends again). Cancel refuses a ready job (409 `job_already_terminal`); the pipeline would otherwise withhold it for good. Status never carries content.
`GET /{jobId}/result` returns candidates only for a ready job while the owner is still the principal the allowlist lists for that upstream and the
pipeline reports delivery current (it re-reads the operator source registry on every call); otherwise `delivery.state` is `withheld` with a
reason code. Delivery is checked at one instant: content already sent cannot be recalled, and a revocation after the check is not observed.

**Review (`relation.review`).** `POST /{jobId}/reviews` records one `allow` or `reject` decision on one relation candidate that is on HOLD. `allow` is the
operator's FINAL approval: it is not a re-verification, it appends the event with effect `approved`, it runs no verifier or model call, and the operation is
terminal (200, `revalidation.state=not_requested`, `next=none`). The pipeline still re-runs the deterministic checks (schema, endpoints, exact citations)
and re-reads the current source rights, so an approval can never override an unsupported candidate, an invalid citation or a withdrawn source
(409 `review_candidate_ineligible`, or the pipeline's own refusal), and it is refused while a model call for the job is in flight (409 `review_call_in_flight`).
The earlier automatic verdict and claim distributions stay in the history unchanged. `reject` excludes. The result then shows
`eligibility.approvalBasis` (`automatic-verifier` or `operator-final-approval` with the reviewer, the deciding event's revision and time): internal audit
metadata, never an application approval or a publication.
The `Idempotency-Key` is the stable operation id and the body is exactly `{relationCandidateId, expectedSourceVersion, expectedSourceRevision, decision}`; the
reviewer is always the authenticated principal and cannot be sent. `sourceVersion` is the job's `inputDigest` and `sourceRevision` is the relation's runtime
event-chain revision as a decimal string, both read from `GET /{jobId}/result`. They are runtime values, never the application's own review revision (the
public decision API's `expectedRevision`), which this service does not see and which must never be forwarded. A new decision is checked against both values
exactly, the revision inside the pipeline's own append transaction, and anything that does not match records nothing: 409 `source_version_conflict` or
`source_revision_conflict`, and a relation that is not on hold is `review_target_not_hold`. The same key and body return the existing operation even after the
relation has moved on; another body is `idempotency_conflict`, another principal's key is `operation_id_unavailable`. `review` says whether the decision is
recorded: `unconfirmed` means the request was reserved but the service has no proof yet that the event was appended (a lost reply included), so retry the same
request, which reads the chain for a marker only this operation can have written and never appends twice. `publication` is always `not_published`.
Operation status is read from the service ledger and carries no content. An operation recorded under the EARLIER contract (where `allow` asked for an
automatic revalidation) is history: it stays readable with `limitation=review_contract_changed`, its `revalidation` is `verified`/`superseded` only where its
stored history settled it and `contract_changed` otherwise, it is never dispatched or resent and never read as an approval, and its key answers 409
`review_contract_changed` while unconfirmed: a NEW decision with a new key at the relation's current revision is how to proceed. This slice has no list route.

**S2 extraction jobs (`/internal/v1/extraction-jobs`, schema `zoop-ai-internal-extraction-1`, scopes `extraction.*`).** A separate family over the
installed `zoop-ai-extract` pipeline: it shares no wire contract, ledger or state machine with S1 or S3, but its children run behind the same
single gate as S3's, so an S2 write and an S3 read of its ledger can never overlap. It is off unless its own all-or-nothing server configuration group is
set (otherwise every route answers 409 `execution_unavailable` after authentication). A caller never sends the S2 `Submit`: the body is exactly
`{schemaVersion: "zoop-extraction-s2-2", jobId, approvedRequestDigest}`. The operator's server-owned approval file maps `principal + jobId +
approvedRequestDigest` to the exact S2 request (snapshot, catalogue, incoming observation, topic request) and EITHER the digests of the authored replay
fixtures it runs against (a replay request) OR the identity of the live runtime binding it may spend money under (`liveRuntimeIdentity`, a request with
`executionMode: live`, `recordingKind: provider`: a real model call, no fixture); anything not listed is 403 `request_not_approved` before a ledger row or child
exists, and the same answer whether or not the job exists. A live approval also needs the service's live group (409 `live_unavailable` otherwise). An approval
only narrows what the pipeline allows: the pipeline still re-reads the operator source registry on every content-bearing command, and, for a live request,
the model-send rights of every document it transmits.
The principal owns the job it submits (another principal's job answers like a missing one) and a job id that already exists in the pipeline ledger is
`job_id_unavailable`: an operator's job is never adopted.

The first reservation freezes the approved digest, the producer fixture digest (replay) or the live runtime identity, the optional topic fixture digest and the
`inputDigest` the pipeline must report (computed from the approved bytes and the pin, not echoed). The same request again keeps all of it; the same job with another
approved digest is `idempotency_conflict`; an approval entry, runtime identity or fixture file that has since changed is `approval_changed` /
`fixture_changed` / `live_binding_changed` (or a withheld result) and the job id is never rebound. The pipeline must freeze a live job under exactly the pinned
identity (409 `live_binding_mismatch` otherwise). The approval is re-read, and the fixtures re-hashed, at submit, at every dispatch, at recover and at delivery.

The initial dispatch runs once, under the pipeline's own under-lock initial-only restriction (a job that already took its first dispatch is refused with no
effect). A child that timed out, died or answered unreadably, and a dispatch left in flight by a restarted service, are never run
again automatically (`next=recover`); a pipeline `extraction_busy`/`ingestion_busy` refusal before any effect is retried a few times, but a job that the
pipeline recorded as `stopped` (for example `ingestion_busy` during execution) waits for an explicit recover. A call the pipeline reserved but never saw
answered ends `reconciling` and is never resent (`reconcile_required`; for a live job the failure is `live_response_unknown`). Only an explicit `recover` dispatches again (and, for a live job, may spend again). Cancel makes a queued, running, stopped or reconciling job `cancelled` for good and
is idempotent; a ready job is refused with 409 `job_already_terminal` and stays ready. Status never carries content. `usage` counts `providerCalls` (transmitted or possibly
transmitted), `receivedCalls`, `unsentCalls` (definitively not sent), reported tokens and the estimated/charged USD (null while unknown): never a guess. `GET /{jobId}/result` returns event
candidates (with their comparisons, citations and disposition) and topic candidates only for a ready job while the pipeline reports delivery current, the
approval is still the reserved one, the fixtures are still the pinned bytes and every receipt was answered by them; otherwise `delivery.state` is
`withheld` with a reason code. Nothing is ever approved by this family: every candidate carries `approved: false`. Delivery is checked at one instant: content
already sent cannot be recalled. Listing a delivered S2 job as an S3 upstream is a separate, explicit operator decision in the S3 allowlist; an S2 result never
widens S3 authority by itself.

**Graph versions (`/internal/v1/graph-versions`, schema `zoop-ai-internal-graph-1`, scope `graph.read`).** A third, separate, strictly read-only family over the
installed `zoop-ai-graph read|focus` pipeline commands: a verified status of one version and the bounded neighbourhood of one company. It writes nothing
(no version, no pointer, no graph ledger, Neo4j or source ledger write, no model call), runs no caller-supplied query and has no list route. It is off unless
its all-or-nothing server configuration group is set (otherwise every route answers 409 `execution_unavailable` after authentication) and it is **not**
public: nothing here activates, publishes or withdraws a version, and `publication` is always `not-published`.

**Which versions a caller may read.** The version id is only a label, so the operator lists per principal the exact `{versionId, graphDigest, payloadDigest}` (and
optionally the frozen S3 relation job as `sourceRelation`) in a server-owned allowlist that is re-read on every request. A version that is not listed answers 403
`version_not_allowed` before any ledger or child process is touched, with one answer for "unknown" and "exists but not yours"; the service never adopts a version
the operator did not list. A listed version that the graph ledger does not have answers 404 `version_not_found` (an operator configuration gap).

**Delivery.** Content leaves only while the version verifies *now*: the pipeline re-checks the S3/S2 authority and source grants, every canonical decision, the S3
review state, the Neo4j store binding and the **full stored graph** against the frozen digest on every call, the digests it reports must equal the listed ones, and
the listed entry must be unchanged when read again just before the response. Otherwise the answer is **200 with `delivery.state=withheld`**, a reason code
(`source_unauthorized`, `upstream_changed`, `canonical_mapping_changed`, `review_revision_changed`, `graph_version_corrupt`, `graph_store_identity_mismatch`,
`version_not_ready`, `version_pin_mismatch`, `source_pin_mismatch` ...) and nothing else: no `verification`, `graph` or `evidence`. A withheld answer is not an
error and not an empty graph. These checks are separate reads at separate instants, so a revocation that lands between them and the response is not covered and
nothing recalls content a caller already received. `current` means "verified now", never "the version the application shows": there is no active pointer.

**Status.** `GET /{versionId}` runs the same gate chain and returns identity, `state` (`frozen|reserved|unknown|ready|failed`), `delivery` and, only when current,
`verification` (graph and payload digests, node and edge counts). It carries no node, edge or evidence and no Issue counts: the graph is built from S3
relations, not from Issues.

**Focus.** `GET /{versionId}/focus?companyId=&depth=` takes exactly these two query parameters, each once; `depth` is exactly 1, 2 or 3 and anything else (an unknown
or repeated key, `01`, `4`, a list) is 422. The neighbourhood is breadth-first over the undirected edges of the verified version; an edge is shown iff one endpoint is
closer than `depth`. `focus.found=false` (with empty `graph.nodes`, `graph.edges` and `evidence`) means the company is not a node of the verified version; it is a
verified answer, not an error. `evidence` lists only the records the shown edges reference, as IDs and document/version/span coordinates: the graph holds no quote,
title, URL, rationale or review note, and none is returned.

**Busy and unavailable.** An operator writer holding a ledger (`graph_busy`, `relation_busy`, `extraction_busy`, `ingestion_busy`) is 503 `runtime_busy`, a graph
database that does not answer is 503 `runtime_unavailable`, unusable server configuration or state (credentials, unbound store, damaged ledger) is 503
`service_configuration_invalid`, and too many concurrent reads is 503 `service_busy`; all carry `Retry-After`. A 503 is never an empty graph.

**Graph handoff bundles (`/internal/v1/graph-handoffs`, schema `zoop-ai-internal-handoff-1`, scope `handoff.read`).** A fourth, separate, strictly read-only
family over the installed `zoop-ai-handoff export` command: the verified status of one AI handoff and, only while it verifies now, the whole versioned bundle
(`zoop-graph-handoff-bundle-5`) the application imports. It is **not** the `graph.read` family above and shares none of its variables, scope or allowlist. It
writes nothing (no handoff, no ledger, no cache, no source write, no model or network call), cannot freeze, recover, activate or publish, runs no caller-supplied
path, command or query and has no list route. It is off unless its all-or-nothing server configuration group is set (otherwise both routes answer 409
`execution_unavailable` after authentication). `publication` is always `not-published` and `appImport` always `pending`: this service delivers the AI-side
artifact; the application's article/text/evidence/catalog verification, snapshot registration and activation are the backend's and are not claimed here.

**Which handoffs a caller may read.** A handoff id is only a label, so the operator lists per principal the exact `{handoffId, manifestDigest, bundleDigest}`
(both SHA-256 pins are required) in a server-owned allowlist that is re-read on every request and again before anything of the answer is used. A handoff that is
not listed for the caller answers 403 `handoff_not_allowed` before any child process is touched, with one answer for "unknown", "exists but not yours" and
"listed for another principal". A listed handoff that the ledger does not have answers 404 `handoff_not_found` (an operator configuration gap).

**Delivery.** Content leaves only while the handoff verifies *now*: the producer re-checks on every export the S3 authority and S2 upstream pins, grants and
rights, the used review revisions, the three operator files against the manifest pins and the rebuilt content digest; the service then hashes the canonical
bytes of the bundle it received, requires the result to equal the producer's receipt **and** the operator's pins, parses it through a closed model (unknown
fields are refused at every level) and requires the model to dump back to exactly those canonical bytes. Otherwise the answer is **200 with
`delivery.state=withheld`**, a reason code (`source_unauthorized`, `upstream_changed`, `source_pin_missing`, `review_revision_changed`,
`canonical_mapping_changed`, `decisions_changed`, `bindings_changed`, `handoff_content_changed`, `handoff_not_ready`, `handoff_pin_mismatch`,
`handoff_contract_changed` ...) and nothing else: no `verification` (so no count, source id or digest) and no `bundle`. `handoff_contract_changed` means the
handoff was frozen under an earlier bundle schema (`zoop-graph-handoff-bundle-1`, `-2`, `-3` or `-4`): it is never reinterpreted or relayed, and the operator freezes a new handoff id.
A withheld answer is not an error and not an empty bundle; do not import it and do not treat it as "no data". The checks are separate reads at separate instants,
so a revocation that lands between them and the response is not covered and nothing recalls content a caller already received.

**Original mentions.** Every `issues[].mentions[]` item is one S2 mention exactly as extracted (`documentId`, `documentVersion` and the S2 local `mentionId`
identify it; a local id is unique only within one document version), with the app article it belongs to and the evidence ids of its own citations. Its
`verification` is always `none`: title, action, target, time, period, assertion status, background flag and participants are candidate or snapshot values of S2,
never verified, decided or approved fields, and they are not derived from the merged issue. A participant carries the S2 `sourceCompanyId`, the S2 `name` and the
S2 `role` text as is (not a confirmed role, not an `INVOLVES` relation); `companyId` is the public company only where every carrying upstream mapped the source id
to the same company of this bundle, otherwise null.

**Field provenance.** Every issue carries a closed `fieldProvenance` that records how the producer chose the issue's six headline values (`title`, `action`,
`target`, `eventTime`, `period`, `assertionStatus`): `selection` is `unanimous` (no operator representative; every mention states all six values) or
`operator-representative` (the operator's single representative decision; it is one choice for all six fields, never a per-field decision). `sameValueMentions`
lists per field, in the order of `mentions[]`, the identities (`documentId`, `documentVersion`, `mentionId`) of exactly those mentions whose own value equals the
issue's value (null equals null; no trimming or time normalisation) where "the issue's value" is the SELECTED value, never a redacted null. `verification` is always
`none`: this is the actual selection, never a fact verification, support or approval. `withheld` lists (`eventTime`, `period` order) the fields whose headline the
producer nulled because of an operator HOLD or REJECT on the selected basis. The producer proves list exactness and closure; this service checks only the shapes.

**Field verdicts.** `issues[].fieldVerdicts` holds the operator's own per-field decisions on one original mention's `eventTime` or `period` (`field`, the exact
reviewed `value`, `decision` ALLOW|HOLD|REJECT, a closed `reasonCode`, `evidenceIds` of the mention's own document, `reviewer`, `decisionRef`, `decisionVersion`,
`verification` always `operator-field-verdict`). They are never AI output, carry no free-text note, and exist only where an operator reviewed; an empty list means
"no field verdict exists", not "verified". This service neither derives nor judges them and checks only the shapes (decision/reason/evidence-count combinations:
ALLOW+stated needs spans, HOLD+unstated none, HOLD+ambiguous spans, REJECT+contradicted spans). Original `mentions[]` values are never changed.

**The bundle bytes.** `bundle` is the producer's artifact, relayed with exactly its keys and values. `verification.bundleDigest` is the SHA-256 of its canonical
UTF-8 bytes, where canonical means JSON with keys sorted by code point, separators `,` and `:` without whitespace and non-ASCII characters not escaped (Python
`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)`). All numbers are non-negative integers and all keys ASCII, so any JSON parser followed by that
serialisation reproduces the same bytes and the same digest, whatever the language; do not normalise, drop or add a field before hashing. Every key the service
adds (`appImport`, `observedAt`, `verification`, `delivery`) is a sibling of `bundle`, never inside it. Strings that came from sources (titles, URLs, labels,
observation and grant metadata, `sourceKind`) are data the producer recorded, never an authority: nothing in them proves or extends a right, and the pins and the
current `delivery.state` are the only delivery gates.

**The manifest bytes.** `manifest` is the operator's frozen manifest exactly as the producer's ledger stored it at freeze time (never rebuilt from today's files or
configuration): schema, handoff id, source-kind declaration, policy version, the S3/S2 source pins with their review digests and the three operator-file SHA-256
hashes. It holds no path and no secret. Its canonical bytes (same canonicalisation as the bundle) hash to `verification.manifestDigest`, which equals
`bundle.manifestDigest`. The service refuses (500 `runtime_binding_mismatch`) a manifest whose digest, handoff id, declaration, policy version, file hashes or
source pins disagree with the bundle or the producer's receipt, and (500 `runtime_contract_mismatch`) a missing manifest or any unknown field at any level. A
backend therefore recomputes both digests from ONE authenticated response. `manifest` is a sibling of `bundle`; status and withheld answers never carry it.

**Status.** `GET /{handoffId}` runs the same full export gate chain and returns identity, `state`, `delivery`, `appImport` and, only when current,
`verification` (manifest, bundle and content digests, bundle size, the bundle's own counts, number of source jobs, provenance declaration). It carries no
node, source id, text or title.

**Bundle.** `GET /{handoffId}/bundle` returns the same fields plus `manifest` and `bundle`. The response is bounded by the producer's 6 MiB bundle limit; the
service reads at most 16 MiB from its child, so an oversized answer is a 503 (`runtime_unavailable`), never a truncated bundle.

**Busy and unavailable.** An operator writer holding a ledger (`handoff_busy`, `relation_busy`, `extraction_busy`, `ingestion_busy`) is 503 `runtime_busy`;
unusable server configuration or operator state (damaged or altered artifact, operator file, ownership, ledger recovery needed) is 503
`service_configuration_invalid`; too many concurrent reads (at most 2 children) is 503 `service_busy`; a missed 45 s deadline or an unreadable answer is 503
`runtime_unavailable`. All carry `Retry-After`; there is exactly one child per request and no automatic retry. A child answer that is not the contract this service
knows is 500 `runtime_contract_mismatch` or `runtime_binding_mismatch` (not retryable). A 503 or 500 is never an empty bundle.

BApprovalBasis.title: BApprovalBasis
BApprovalBasis.description:
Why one S3 relation was eligible when the producer used it: the automatic verifier's verdict (`reviewer` null) or an operator's final approval
(`reviewer` the approving principal). `revision` is the deciding chain event's sequence.

BArticleOrigin.title: BArticleOrigin
BArticleOrigin.description: The operator's declared origin of one article version (never inferred from a publisher, domain or source id).

BFieldProvenance.title: BFieldProvenance
BFieldProvenance.description:
How the producer chose the issue's six headline values: `unanimous` (every mention states them) or `operator-representative` (the operator's single
representative decision). `verification` is always `none`: this is the actual selection, never a verification, support or approval of any value.
`withheld` lists the fields (`eventTime`, `period` order) whose headline the producer set to null because of an operator HOLD or REJECT.

BFieldVerdict.title: BFieldVerdict
BFieldVerdict.description:
An operator's per-field verdict on one original mention's `eventTime` or `period` value, exactly as reviewed. Shape only: the producer owns binding,
evidence closure, order and the effect on the issue's headline. There is no free-text reason and never AI output.

BMention.title: BMention
BMention.description:
One original S2 mention of the issue, identified by its source document version and S2 local id (a local id is unique only within one document version).
`verification` is always `none`: these are S2 candidate or snapshot values, never verified, decided or approved fields.

BMentionRef.title: BMentionRef
BMentionRef.description: The identity of one original mention of the same issue (a reference, never a copy of its values).

BParticipant.title: BParticipant
BParticipant.description:
A participant exactly as the S2 mention states it. `role` is the S2 text, never a confirmed role; `company_id` is the public company id only where every
carrying upstream mapped `source_company_id` to the same company of this bundle, otherwise null.

BReviewUse.title: BReviewUse
BReviewUse.description: The chain revision of one relation the bundle used, with the basis that made it eligible (`approvalBasis.revision` equals `revision`).

BSameValueMentions.title: BSameValueMentions
BSameValueMentions.description:
Per headline field, the mentions whose own value equals the issue's value exactly (null equals null, no normalisation). Shape only: the producer owns the
exactness, order and closure of these lists.

BSourceProvenance.title: BSourceProvenance
BSourceProvenance.description: The execution provenance of ONE S3 source job. Every source of a bundle carries exactly the bundle's own triple (the producer withholds a mix).

BSourceSupport.title: BSourceSupport
BSourceSupport.description:
How many independent sources the issue's cited article versions represent. `knownLineageCount` counts lineage groups that have a declared origin
(never articles), `duplicateGroups` are groups of articles whose prepared text is exactly equal (never transitive components) and
`independentSourceCount` is null whenever an origin is missing or conflicting. Shape only: the producer owns every count.

BStructuralComplete.title: BStructuralComplete
BStructuralComplete.description: An ordered chain [participant, (mapped middle,) target] with one directed supplier→customer link per S3 basis. Operator-mapped basis chain only.

Bundle.title: Bundle
Bundle.description: The producer's artifact. Key names, order-free content and every value are the producer's; this class only says which shapes are acceptable.

CallReceipt.title: CallReceipt
CallReceipt.description: Per-attempt accounting metadata. It carries no provider receipt, response content, request payload or fixture identity.

EcCitation.title: EcCitation
EcCitation.description: An exact, source-mapped quote. The artifact id, raw locator ids and source segment table the pipeline also stores are not relayed.

EcDocument.title: EcDocument
EcDocument.description: The immutable document identity. The raw-bytes version the pipeline also stores is not relayed.

EcMention.title: EcMention
EcMention.description: The replay model's mention. Its own evidence list is not relayed (the candidate's verified `citations` are).

ExtractionJobContent.title: ExtractionJobContent
ExtractionJobContent.description: The delivered candidates of one ready job. Nothing here is approved: `approved` is false on every candidate.

ExtractionReceipt.title: ExtractionReceipt
ExtractionReceipt.description: Per-call accounting metadata: no request/response digest, fixture hash or content.

ExtractionUsage.title: ExtractionUsage
ExtractionUsage.description:
Accounting. `providerCalls` counts calls transmitted or possibly transmitted (a started call without receipt included), `receivedCalls` the
ones a reply was stored for, `unsentCalls` the ones definitively NOT sent. A replay job reports 0/null for the live-only fields.

found.title: Found
found.description: Whether the company is a node of the verified version. null while delivery is withheld.

distance.title: Distance
distance.description: Undirected hop distance from the focus company (0 for the company itself).

GraphVerification.title: GraphVerification
GraphVerification.description: What the pipeline verified for this very response: the stored graph is exactly the frozen one. Digests and counts only.

HandoffManifest.title: HandoffManifest
HandoffManifest.description:
The operator's frozen manifest exactly as the producer's ledger stores it (closed at every level): pins and file hashes only, no path or secret.
Its canonical JSON bytes hash to `verification.manifestDigest` and to the bundle's `manifestDigest`.

HdBundle.title: HdBundle
HdBundle.description:
The status fields plus the frozen `manifest` and the whole `bundle`, only while delivery is current. `manifest` and `bundle` are the producer's own
artifacts exactly: the canonical JSON bytes of `manifest` hash to `verification.manifestDigest` (= `bundle.manifestDigest`), those of `bundle` to
`verification.bundleDigest`, so the application can recompute both from this one response. Nothing the service adds is part of either; every
service field is a sibling.

checkedAt.title: Checkedat
checkedAt.description: The producer's own time of the current-authority check. null while withheld.

bundleDigest.title: Bundledigest
bundleDigest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical UTF-8 bytes of the bundle; equals the operator's pin.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Number of S3 source jobs the handoff was frozen from.

HdVerification.title: HdVerification
HdVerification.description: What was verified for this very response: digests of the received bytes and the counts the bundle itself reports. No source id, text or title.

RcApprovalBasis.title: RcApprovalBasis
RcApprovalBasis.description: Why a relation is `eligible`: the automatic verifier's verdict or the operator's final approval, with the deciding chain event.

RcEvent.title: RcEvent
RcEvent.description: One append-only chain entry. Reviewer and note are free text from operator CLI reviews and are never relayed.

sourceVersion.title: Sourceversion
sourceVersion.description: The runtime job's `inputDigest`: send it back as `expectedSourceVersion`. Immutable for the job.

sourceRevision.title: Sourcerevision
sourceRevision.description: This relation's runtime event-chain revision (the same number as `eligibility.revision`, as a decimal string): send it back as `expectedSourceRevision`. Not the application's review revision.

RelationJobContent.title: RelationJobContent
RelationJobContent.description: The delivered candidates of one ready job. `approved` is always false: `eligible` is the automatic evidence gate, not publication.

RelationOperationStatus.title: RelationOperationStatus
RelationOperationStatus.description: One review operation, identified exactly by the caller's Idempotency-Key. Content-free; read from the service ledger.

RelationPublicationPhase.title: RelationPublicationPhase
RelationPublicationPhase.description: Publication is never done by this service: the relation stays unpublished whatever the verdict says.

RelationReceipt.title: RelationReceipt
RelationReceipt.description: Per-call accounting metadata: no request/response digest, fixture identity or content.

RelationRevalidationPhase.title: RelationRevalidationPhase
RelationRevalidationPhase.description:
Legacy only. A final approval (`allow`) or exclusion (`reject`) requests no revalidation (`not_requested`). The two other states describe an
operation recorded under the earlier contract, where an `allow` asked for an automatic re-check: `verified`/`superseded` are what its stored
history settled, `contract_changed` that it never settled and never will (nothing is dispatched or resent).

RelationReviewPhase.title: RelationReviewPhase
RelationReviewPhase.description:
Acceptance: whether the decision is recorded in the AI relation ledger. `unconfirmed` means the request was reserved but the service has no
proof yet that the event was appended; retry the same request (same key and body) to reconcile it.

jobId.title: Jobid
jobId.description: An operator-prepared S2 extraction job. It must be listed for the calling principal in the server-owned allowlist.

job.description: The runtime `get` payload for the importer, present only when delivery.state is available.

RelationSubmit.description: The S3 `Submit` contract (`zoop-relation-s3`). Fixtures, registries and paths cannot be named. `executionMode: live` is accepted only for an upstream the operator listed as live-approved.
RelationSubmit.title: RelationSubmit

RelationReview.description:
One review decision on one relation candidate. The path names the job and the Idempotency-Key is the stable operation id. The reviewer
is the authenticated principal and cannot be sent; nothing here is the application's own review revision.

expectedSourceVersion.description: The job's `sourceVersion`: its `inputDigest`, as read from the result or status.
expectedSourceVersion.title: Expectedsourceversion

expectedSourceRevision.description: The relation's `sourceRevision` as read from the result: the runtime's event-chain revision as a decimal string. Never the application's own revision.
expectedSourceRevision.title: Expectedsourcerevision

RelationReview.title: RelationReview

ExtractionSubmit.description:
The S2 submit reference. It names a request the operator preapproved for this principal; it carries no snapshot, catalogue, observation,
path, fixture or live mode, and the pipeline's `Submit` body is never accepted from a caller.

jobId.description: Equals the Idempotency-Key. The server-owned approval is looked up by this principal and job id.
jobId.title: Jobid

approvedRequestDigest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the operator-approved S2 request. It must be the digest the operator listed for this principal and job id.
approvedRequestDigest.title: Approvedrequestdigest

ExtractionSubmit.title: ExtractionSubmit

bearerAuth.description: Operator-issued token; the service holds only its SHA-256 digest. Roles are the route scopes.

servers.description: Loopback only. Never exposed directly; reach it through a co-located TLS proxy.
